headline: Spatial omics resolves niche communication, recruitment, and multiscale tissue topology
label: Spatial Single Cell Profiling
summary: Spatial omics methods now infer communication motifs, niche recruitment, and perturbation phenotypes directly in tissue context.
synthesis: The dominant thread is spatially resolved inference of tissue organization from transcriptomic and multimodal imaging data. ALARMIST infers multicellular ligand-receptor communication motifs in LUAD/AIS and glioma, ClusToRa uses a fixed-position null model to detect recruitment and infiltration with reduced false-positive enrichment, and COSTE embeds directed nearest-neighbor distance profiles to quantify multiscale topology. SPAC-seq and TARDIS couple spatial CRISPR screening to phenotypes, a pan-cancer atlas maps tertiary lymphoid structures across 12 cancers, and MIAAIM integrates histology, imaging mass cytometry, and mass spectrometry imaging. Non-spatial work, including SuperSCC hierarchical clustering across 90+ scRNA-seq datasets, SIGnature gene-importance scoring from foundation model attributions, and metabolic flux inference in pancreatic cancer, is adjacent rather than shared. What is new is niche-level and perturbation-level readout resolved in space, with inference anchored to tissue context.
